p: Camden has a big personality, and it's worth leaning into it before you pick up a ball. Camden Lock, where the markets meet Regent's Canal, is the beating heart of the area, and narrowboats chug through the locks while crowds browse the stalls. The Roundhouse, a converted Victorian railway engine shed, is one of London's most distinctive music and arts venues, so check what's on if you fancy combining a game with a gig.

Regent's Park is a short walk away, with its beautifully kept gardens, boating lake and Queen Mary's Gardens, famous for their roses in early summer. It's the perfect calm before the competitive storm.

Bowling tips for the less experienced: choose a ball that fits your hand comfortably and that you can swing without straining. Aim for the arrows on the lane rather than the pins, and follow through towards your target. Mix experienced and new bowlers across teams so the game stays close, and set a fun forfeit for the losing side.

Getting there is easy: Camden Town and Chalk Farm Tube stations on the Northern line serve the area, and Camden Road Overground isn't far. Just be warned that Camden Town station can get very crowded at weekends, so pick a meeting point outside and give yourself a bit of extra time if you're meeting friends.
